faq.question: What is SsaveVideo and how does it work?
faq.answer: SsaveVideo is a free web tool that turns a public video link into direct download buttons. It asks the source platform for the media manifest, picks the formats available to a logged-out visitor and returns their addresses; your browser then fetches the file from the platform's own content delivery network.

faq.question: Which sites are supported?
faq.answer: YouTube including Shorts and MP3-style audio, TikTok, Instagram Reels and Stories, Facebook Watch and Reels, Reddit, Pinterest, Threads and X (Twitter). Paste any supported link and the correct extractor is selected from the URL automatically.

faq.question: Is it free, and are there limits?
faq.answer: Everything is free with no account, no paywall and no daily download quota. There is a per-IP rate limit on the lookup endpoint, which keeps the service fast for everyone and is not a cap on how much you can save.

faq.question: Do you keep a copy of the videos I download?
faq.answer: No. The server stores media never — not temporarily, not cached, not logged. Only the resolved URL lives in your browser's memory for as long as the result card is open.

faq.question: Why does a link sometimes fail?
faq.answer: Because the video is private, deleted, region-restricted or age-gated, or because the platform is briefly unreachable. The error message tells you which one it was so you know whether to fix the link or leave it.

faq.question: Can I use it on mobile?
faq.answer: Yes. The page is mobile-first and works in Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge and Brave on Android and iPhone, where long-pressing a format button saves the file to your device.

guides.name: No-watermark guide
guides.meta_title: How to Download Videos Without a Watermark | SsaveVideo
guides.meta_description: A downloader watermark means your file was re-encoded. Here is why the overlay appears, what it costs in bitrate, and how a tool avoids it entirely.
guides.h1: How to Download Videos Without a Watermark
guides.intro: A watermark on a downloaded video is not proof of anything — it is a second render. This guide explains where the overlay comes from, why it costs you quality, and what a genuine watermark-free download actually means.

sections.title: Where the logo comes from
sections.body: A downloader that stamps your file has to decode the source, composite its branding and encode the result again. That means the video passes through a server, a GPU or your own browser twice, and every encoder introduces loss. The logo is a marketing decision paid for with your bitrate.

sections.title: Why the platform watermark is different
sections.body: TikTok and a few others publish two renditions of the same upload: one with the scrolling handle baked into the master, and a clean one used by their own players. Tools that only know the public share URL often grab the stamped copy. SsaveVideo asks the extractor for the media manifest and prefers the unbranded stream that the platform itself plays.

sections.title: The architecture that avoids it
sections.body: Our server never downloads media. It resolves the signed CDN address for a format and hands that URL to your browser, which pulls the bytes from the platform. No re-encode happens anywhere in the chain, so the file is identical to the original stream, minus nothing and plus nothing.

sections.title: When you still cannot avoid it
sections.body: If a clip only exists as a burned-in version — some cross-posted TikTok edits and watermarked stock previews — no tool can remove it without cropping or inpainting. In those cases the honest answer is to reach out to the creator for the master file rather than shipping a degraded crop.

faq.question: Is a watermark-free download the same quality?
faq.answer: Yes, because it is the same bytes. Since nothing is re-encoded, you keep the source resolution, codec and bitrate exactly as the platform published them.

faq.question: Can I remove a watermark from a video I already saved?
faq.answer: Only badly. Cropping changes the composition, blurring and inpainting leave artefacts, and any fix re-encodes the file. Re-downloading the original clean stream is a better outcome than editing the stamped copy.

faq.question: Do I need a premium plan to avoid watermarks here?
faq.answer: No. There are no plans and no upsells on SsaveVideo. Every output on every supported platform is watermark-free because the pipeline has no way to add branding.

guides.name: Separate tracks explained
guides.meta_title: Silent Video Download? Fix Separate A/V Tracks | SsaveVideo
guides.meta_description: Adaptive streaming keeps picture and sound as two separate tracks, so saved clips end up mute. Here is how to pick the merged file in one click.
guides.h1: Your Downloaded Video Has No Sound — Here Is Why
guides.intro: One of the most common complaints about any downloader is a silent MP4. The cause is almost never the tool: it is how adaptive streaming splits a master into picture and sound.

sections.title: How adaptive streaming splits media
sections.body: YouTube, Reddit, TikTok and Facebook publish DASH or HLS manifests where video and audio are distinct representations. The player fetches both and merges them on your device in real time, which lets a viewer change quality without restarting and lets the platform encode a silent 4K video stream more cheaply.

sections.title: Why naive downloaders fail
sections.body: A downloader that simply takes the first URL in the manifest usually gets the picture-only representation. The file is valid, plays instantly and has no audio track at all — which is why the same clip looks fine in the browser and mute on your phone.

sections.title: Progressive formats are the fix
sections.body: Most platforms also publish a progressive rendition, where the encoder muxed audio and video into one container. Selecting it, as Reddit's profile in our schema forces, gives you a single file that plays everywhere. SsaveVideo sorts results by combined tracks first and explicitly labels anything video-only.

sections.title: When merging really is required
sections.body: Some high resolutions exist only as split streams, and combining them needs ffmpeg and a server-side pass over the media. That costs bandwidth, storage and time, and it is the reason most free tools cap quality at 720p. We choose speed and original fidelity instead: you keep the separate stream, and a desktop editor such as HandBrake or ffmpeg can merge it locally whenever you want.

faq.question: How do I check whether a file has an audio track?
faq.answer: Right-click the file and open Properties or Get Info, or drag it into VLC and check Codec Information. If no audio stream is listed, the source row was video-only.

faq.question: Can I merge video and audio myself without losing quality?
faq.answer: Yes. ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -i audio.m4a -c copy merged.mp4 remuxes both streams without re-encoding, so it finishes in seconds with zero generation loss.

faq.question: Why is 4K only offered as a separate video stream?
faq.answer: At that bitrate the platform wants bandwidth to scale with the viewer's connection, so picture and sound are negotiated independently. Merging them server-side for every request would be the most expensive operation a download service can run.

guides.name: Safety guide
guides.meta_title: Is It Safe to Download Videos Online? | SsaveVideo
guides.meta_description: Most risk on converter sites is not the video but the traps around it: fake installers, push prompts and credential forms. Here are the checks that matter.
guides.h1: Is It Safe to Download Videos Online?
guides.intro: Most risk on converter sites is not the video — it is everything wrapped around it. Here are the checks that matter before you paste a link anywhere.

sections.title: Never run the installer it offers
sections.body: If a site claims your download will start faster after installing a helper, downloader or browser extension, close the tab. A web page has no legitimate reason to ship you an executable, and that binary is how adware and infostealers reach a machine.

sections.title: Watch for push-notification traps
sections.body: Sites that show a button reading Allow notifications are buying the right to put ads on your desktop hours later. No download flow needs notifications; deny them and clear the permission in your browser settings if you already clicked.

sections.title: Check what the domain can read
sections.body: A downloader that asks you to log in to the source platform, or to paste cookies or an API token, is collecting credentials and a session that outlives the download. A tool that works only on public links is not merely limited — it is safer by construction.

sections.title: Prefer HTTPS direct links, and use them fast
sections.body: Signed CDN addresses expire in minutes by design, which protects the platform but also means a copied link is a temporary artefact, not a permanent one. Save to your device rather than forwarding raw links, and never paste a signed link into a public chat where anyone can follow it.

sections.title: Respect the copyright line
sections.body: Safety is also legal: downloading your own uploads and openly licensed media is unremarkable, while republishing someone else's footage is not. Keep a licence note with anything you archive for work so provenance is documented later.

faq.question: Does SsaveVideo store the links I paste?
faq.answer: Extraction runs in memory and the resolved media URLs are discarded once the request ends. The only thing retained is an anonymised error counter used to keep the service up, and no media bytes ever touch our disk.

faq.question: Is HTTPS enough to make a download safe?
faq.answer: Transport encryption is the baseline, not the whole answer. What matters is that the file is a media container served by a known content delivery network and not a signed executable from a random host.

faq.question: Can a website infect my phone through a video download?
faq.answer: Barely, and usually only with help. iOS and Android sandbox downloads from the browser, so the realistic risk is a social step: installing a profile, a side-loaded app or an update prompt the site invents. Decline every such request and the download itself is fine.

guides.name: Choosing quality
guides.meta_title: 1080p or 4K: Which Quality to Download | SsaveVideo
guides.meta_description: Resolution alone decides nothing. Compare bitrate, codec and file size, and learn which rendition to take for editing, casting or an offline trip.
guides.intro: Downloading the highest number is nearly always wrong. Resolution is one input to file size, and the codec that carries it decides whether the clip looks good or clogs your storage.

sections.title: Resolution is not quality
sections.body: A 2160p stream at 8 Mbps looks worse than a 1080p stream at 12 Mbps, because detail is limited by data per second, not pixels per frame. This is why SsaveVideo prints the measured bitrate and container next to every row: two files with the same label can differ by a factor of three.

sections.title: Codecs: H.264 versus VP9 and AV1
sections.body: MP4 with H.264 plays on everything, including older consoles, TVs and editors. VP9 and AV1 in WebM are far more efficient at the same quality but need hardware support, and some editors refuse or transpose them badly. For archiving take the most efficient stream; for editing and casting take MP4.

sections.title: Rule of thumb by use case
sections.body: Phone viewing and offline travel: 720p MP4. Cutting into a project: highest MP4 you can store. Reference archive of a tutorial: 1080p or 4K regardless of size. Audio-only: the top audio row, since a talk track needs no picture at all and the saving is enormous.

sections.title: Reading the result card
sections.body: Each row shows label, container, height, frame rate, bitrate and approximate size, and rows marked merged already contain audio. Where the platform caps uploads — TikTok at 1080p, Reddit at 1080p — you will never see a fake 4K option, because we only list what genuinely exists for that video.

faq.question: Does a bigger file always mean better quality?
faq.answer: No. Beyond the point where the codec stops discarding detail, extra size is usually duplicate information. Match the rendition to the source: a 720p upload never becomes better by taking a padded 1080p representation.

faq.question: Which format should I choose for editing?
faq.answer: MP4 with H.264 for maximum compatibility in Premiere, Final Cut and DaVinci Resolve. HEVC in MP4 is lighter on disk but asks more of your CPU, and WebM support still varies between editors.

faq.question: How much space does an hour of video take?
faq.answer: Roughly 450 MB at 1 Mbps, 1.1 GB at 2.5 Mbps and 4.3 GB at 10 Mbps, since one byte is eight bits and an hour is 3600 seconds. SsaveVideo shows an estimate per row so you can judge before committing.
